title: Traffic Lights & Filter Arrows
whatItIs: Traffic lights follow the same sequence everywhere: red, red and amber, green, amber, then red again.

keyFacts.text: Red: you MUST stop behind the white stop line.

keyFacts: Red and amber: stop, and don't go until green shows.
Green: you may go if the way is clear and there is room for you to clear the junction.
Amber: stop, unless you've already crossed the line or stopping might cause a collision.
A green filter arrow lets you go in that direction, even if the main green light isn't showing.

keyFacts.text: At an advanced stop line, you MUST stop at the first white line when the light is amber or red.

items.label: Green
items.meaning: Go if the way is clear.

items.label: Amber
items.meaning: Stop, unless it is unsafe to do so.

a.label: Red and amber
points: Still means stop: green is next

onTheTest.question: The traffic lights show red and amber together. What should you do?
options: Go if the junction is clear
Speed up before it turns red
Go only if you are turning left
onTheTest.why: Red and amber means stop. Don't move off until the green light shows.

traps: Red and amber is not 'get ready to go': it still means stop.
A green light doesn't give you priority over people already crossing.
Don't move forward on green if you can't clear the junction.
